messages:
sam: quick thread — i sketched a follow-up to the eviction/kv-prefetch rfc. thinking of a shadow "eviction-observability checker" that runs alongside rollout to surface correctness regressions without affecting live decisions. thoughts?

maria: ++ we need more visibility before we flip any global policy. what does the checker observe? metrics or diffs?

sam: both. basic idea: for a sample of prefixes we run the new eviction decision logic (in read-only shadow mode) and compare outcome to current live behavior. capture trace, decision path, relevant lease/epoch ids.
jin: sampling rate and perf impact are the hard parts. if it touches hot prefixes we could add noise to telemetry or overload the tracing pipeline.
maria: agree. prefer adaptive sampling — heavier on low-qps tenants and cold prefixes. also store a compact diff rather than full kv snapshots.
diego: watch out for races: shadow checker might see a prefix mid-handoff and claim a mismatch when the live path eventually wins. we need canonical event anchors (lease epochs).
kate: could we attach a generation id to each prefix snapshot? checker compares on same generation boundary, ignore deltas outside that window. avoids false positives from in-flight handoffs.
sam: exact — propose: attach (prefix, gen, lease_epoch) triple to each sample. require identical anchor to count as a true mismatch. non-anchor mismatches become "timing" cases and are sampled separately.
jin: what about memory? storing k-v snapshots even compact for many samples adds up. maybe store a small bloom of keys and top-k hot keys + hash of value batches.
maria: or leverage our existing prefix telemetry: we already ingest top-keys per-minute. combine that with a small checksum of prefix state. cheaper than full snapshot.
diego: integration with the handoff stream is important. checker should subscribe to the same event bus that records demote/claim/freeze events so it can align anchors reliably.
sam: ops-bot: any objections to using the demote/claim stream as canonical anchor?
ops-bot: deploy-bot: smoke test for evict-observer scheduled in staging at 2024-11-05T09:00Z. No active incidents. :white_check_mark:

kate: one more thought on actionability — we should classify mismatches by severity: correctness (data loss risk), perf (extra tokens), and flakiness (transient timing). map each class to an owner + playbook.
maria: +1. and keep a retention window for raw traces (48h) and aggregated deltas (90d). helps postmortems without bloating storage.
jin: gating rule for rollout: if correctness mismatch rate > 0.5% for two consecutive hours on a nontrivial sample, auto-rollback or pause rollout. we'll need to tune thresholds.
diego: add an instrumentation flag in the runtime to annotate decisions with reason codes. makes diffs easier to interpret.
sam: i'll update the RFC with the sampling algo, anchor rules, and rollback thresholds. volunteers to run the staging smoke and collect initial baselines?
maria: i'll run staging smoke and validate the storage format.
jin: i'll help with the rollout gating code and alerts.
kate: i'll write the initial playbook for mismatch triage.
ops-bot: note: when you file the follow-up RFC PR, tag @eng-sre and include the sample dataset link.
sam: thanks everyone — i'll post the draft PR in ~2h.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: staging smoke completed — no regressions observed in 1h baseline run. :rocket:
